newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran inflation slows to 17.7 percent.
newsitem.headline: Iran inflation slows to 17.7 percent.

text.p: Consumer inflation in Iranian cities slowed to an annual rate of 17.7 percent in the month to May 21, versus 26.4 percent in the same month last year, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported on Sunday.
Quoting a Central Bank of Iran statistics report, IRNA said prices rose by a month-on-month 2.3 percent in the period.
Inflation in the last Iranian year to March 1997 stood at 23.2 percent against 49.4 percent the year before, the central bank governor said earlier this month.

Steep price rises are a common complaint and the government has come under attack in the press and parliament for not doing enough to fight inflation, which Iranian officials have said is a top priority.
